value: Zier, M., Stenzel, P., Kotzur, L., Stolten, D. (2021). A review of decarbonization options for the glass industry. Energy Conversion and Management: X 10, 100083. doi:10.1016/j.ecmx.2021.100083.

Review paper, Germany-centred (German container and flat glass sector averages, EU ETS benchmarks). Loaded: furnace types (regenerative end-port and side-port, recuperative, oxy-fuel, all-electric, hybrid, hydrogen-fired, microwave and plasma TRL) with the numbers the paper prints (capacity ranges, thermal efficiency 45% regenerative end-port and 85% electric for a 300 t/d container furnace, Table B2 SEC examples 3.62 and 6.48 GJ/t, authors assumed electric SEC 2.5 and 4.48 GJ/t, TRLs from Table 11); waste-heat options (cullet, batch-and-cullet preheating, thermochemical heat recovery, ORC, steam turbine, thermoelectric with Table 9 capex per kW electric); the printed fuel-saving percentages as measures. NOT loaded: any absolute furnace capex or opex - the paper states CAPEX and fixed OPEX only qualitatively (Table 6 symbols, Table 10 colour-coded figure, Fig. 18 variable-OPEX bars read from charts; fixed OPEX deliberately not analysed); a numeric SEC for oxy-fuel, hybrid, hydrogen and recuperative furnaces (only relative changes); Fig. 3, 7, 17, 18, B1, B2 chart values. Traps: (1) Table B2 SEC are single illustrative furnaces in the authors model, not sector averages; (2) the electric SEC (2.5 and 4.48 GJ/t) and the constant-SEC hydrogen switch are model ASSUMPTIONS; (3) oxy-fuel 10% and 20% gains are furnace-balance only (excluding oxygen production); (4) Table 3 emission factors are German sector averages incl. cullet effects, kept in other-values; (5) Table 9 capex are for 2020 per kW electric and exclude auxiliaries for steam turbines; (6) the PDF text layer splits several tables into column fragments - Tables 2, 3, 5, 7, 8, 9, 11, B1-B3 were read from the layout-preserving text. Locator: printed page numbers (equal PDF pages).
